newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes drop off in volatile activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes drop off in volatile activity.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes dropped off in volatile activity Monday afternoon as many market players began rolling over their February contracts ahead of Tuesday's NYMEX expiry, traders said.
February West Texas Intermediate was trading around $25.05-15 a barrel, down some 50 cents from this morning and 30 cents from late Friday's cash market.

The February/March WTI spread narrowed by around 20-25 cents from this morning to 65-70 cents a barrel, bringing WTI/Cushing Posting Plus in with it. Postings was trading around $2.50 a barrel, down 35 cents from this morning.
Grade activity was light on this partial U.S. holiday in commemoration of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. The NYMEX is open for a regular session, but some traders took a long weekend.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at WTI/Cushing minus 12 cents, up eight to 11 cents from late Friday.
WTI/Midland was steady to slightly weaker at around WTI/Cushing minus 35 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland weakened to trade at a discount of $1.80 a barrel, down 10 cents from this morning and late Friday's activity.

Imports from the North Sea and West Africa continue to pressure domestic grades. The spread between North Sea Brent and WTI for March stood around $1.70 a barrel, giving sellers ample economic invcentive to maintain steady transatlantic flows.
